sessions.loadingListDescription: Reading local transcript summaries for the current agent view.

toolFilter.label: Minimum duration
toolFilter.emptyTitle: No slow tool calls in this range
toolFilter.emptyDescription: Lower the duration filter to include faster calls.

toolTips.agent: Runs a subagent in a separate context. Its duration includes the delegated task, so it is often longer than one direct tool call.
toolTips.askUser: Shows structured questions and waits for your answer. Long duration usually means the agent was blocked on human input.
toolTips.shell: Runs a shell command in the local environment. Long duration usually comes from tests, builds, installs, network calls, or watch commands.
toolTips.fileRead: Reads local files or resources so the agent can inspect current state before deciding what to do next.
toolTips.fileWrite: Creates or edits files. Failures often mean the file changed since it was read, or the exact edit target did not match.
toolTips.fileSearch: Searches files, symbols, or document text. It is usually cheap, but broad patterns over large trees can still be slow.
toolTips.web: Uses web search or fetch. Duration depends on network latency, provider limits, redirects, and page extraction.
toolTips.skill: Loads a skill instruction bundle. The useful signal is which workflow shaped the agent's later steps.
toolTips.tasks: Updates the agent's task or todo state. These calls explain planning state, not application behavior.
toolTips.patch: Applies a code patch through the local editing helper. Short duration usually means the patch matched cleanly.
toolTips.mcp: Calls an external MCP or plugin tool. Duration includes the connector and the remote or local service behind it.
toolTips.browser: Controls a browser or Playwright session for UI inspection and verification.
toolTips.image: Reads or attaches an image so the agent can inspect visual evidence.
toolTips.workspace: Loads bundled workspace runtimes or document helpers used by local tools.
toolTips.multiAgent: Coordinates another local agent process. Duration can include queueing and the other agent's work.
toolTips.hook: Runs hook-related logic around the session or a tool call.
toolTips.plan: Switches plan-mode state or asks for plan approval before code changes continue.
toolTips.generic: Transcript tool event. Check the summary, file path, status, and duration for the useful signal.

checkpointSummary.noDetailsDescription: Checkpoints are file-history snapshots. This transcript records the count, but does not include the changed files or diff for each checkpoint.

points.scope: A session belongs to one local agent history, but the project grouping helps compare Claude Code and Codex work together.
points.review: Open a detail page when you need transcript-derived assets, tool events, artifacts, or file checkpoints.

memories.title: Memory notes across sources
memories.summary: Berth groups native memory files and durable local notes so you can see which long-lived facts may shape future sessions.

points.role: Use memory notes for durable facts, decisions, and preferences that should survive beyond one chat.
points.scope: Source type tells you whether a note comes from native agent memory, repository guidance, or a local memory store.
points.review: Review stale or high-priority notes when the agent keeps following outdated context.

providers.claude: Claude Code memory files can hold user and project context.
providers.codex: Codex receives durable repository guidance through AGENTS.md and imported instructions.
providers.abstract: Berth also groups local memory notes that are not tied to one provider.

sources.title: Source types
sources.body: Different sources have different loading rules. Treat the source as part of the meaning, not just a storage path.

priority.title: Priority matters
priority.body: Core notes are stronger context than archive notes. They should be rare and regularly reviewed.

review.title: Keep it current
review.body: Memory is useful only while it stays true. Old decisions and temporary preferences should not become permanent rules.

conventions.title: Persistent instruction context
conventions.summary: Instruction files are durable guidance the agent loads as context before work. They carry project rules, team norms, personal preferences, and imports into the first turn.

points.role: Use them for facts and rules that should shape many tasks, not for one-off prompts.
points.scope: Scope tells you who receives the instruction: one user, this project, or an organization policy.
points.review: Check imports and precedence when the agent follows unexpected guidance.

providers.claude: Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md files into the working context.
providers.codex: Codex reads AGENTS.md as repository instructions before work starts.

skills.title: Reusable workflow packages
skills.summary: Skills package repeatable procedures with instructions and optional files. The agent loads the body only when the skill is relevant, so long procedures do not always sit in context.

points.role: The same concept can be backed by Claude Code skills, Codex skill config, or another provider's packaged capability.
points.scope: User skills travel across projects; project skills document team workflow and can be versioned with the repo.
points.review: Read the skill instructions and bundled scripts before trusting a third-party skill.

providers.claude: Claude Code skills are SKILL.md packages loaded when relevant or invoked directly.
providers.codex: Codex skills follow the same packaged-procedure idea through its skill support.

subagents.title: Specialized worker profiles
subagents.summary: Subagents are named agent roles with their own instructions, tools, and sometimes model choices. The main agent can delegate focused work to them instead of keeping every role in one prompt.

points.role: Use them when a repeatable task needs a narrower role, such as review, exploration, or research.
points.scope: Provider support differs, but the abstract asset is a delegated worker definition.
points.review: Check tool access, model settings, and trigger descriptions before relying on delegation.

providers.claude: Claude Code subagents are markdown worker profiles with their own role and tool access.
providers.codex: Codex subagents describe delegated workers that can be invoked by the main session.

commands.title: Saved prompt entry points
commands.summary: Commands are named prompts or procedures that users invoke directly. They are useful when a workflow should start from an explicit action instead of automatic skill selection.

points.role: Use commands for repeatable interactive actions such as release prep, review, or project setup.
points.scope: Personal commands help one user; project commands create shared team shortcuts.
points.review: Check argument handling and any shell snippets before running commands from another source.

providers.claude: Claude Code treats custom commands and skills as explicit slash entry points.
providers.codex: Codex slash commands are named CLI actions and prompts invoked from the session.

outputModes.title: Primary agent behavior styles
outputModes.summary: Output modes adjust how the primary agent responds. They change tone, teaching level, or working style without adding a separate worker.

points.role: Use them when the same task should be handled in a different communication or teaching mode.
points.scope: They are usually local to one user or project because teams may want different interaction styles.
points.review: Treat output modes as behavior policy, not as capability or permission grants.

providers.claude: Claude Code output styles change how the primary agent responds.
providers.abstract: Berth treats this as response behavior policy, not as a tool or worker.

agentTeams.title: Multi-agent composition
agentTeams.summary: Agent teams describe how several agent roles should work together. Berth treats them as orchestration assets rather than a single prompt or tool.

points.role: Use them for structured handoffs where multiple roles repeatedly appear together.
points.scope: Team assets are provider-specific today, but the abstract model is a reusable collaboration plan.
points.review: Check each member role and shared tool access before trusting the combined workflow.

providers.claude: Claude Code can compose agent roles into repeatable team workflows.
providers.abstract: Berth models this as orchestration across worker definitions.

intro.title: Status lines show live session state
intro.all: Claude Code and Codex both expose a status line, but they work differently. Claude Code runs a configured command and renders its output. Codex renders an ordered list of built-in footer items from config.toml.
intro.claude: Claude Code status lines are command-backed settings from settings.json. The command can be a script or inline shell command, and Claude Code refreshes it during the session.
intro.codex: Codex status lines are built-in TUI footer items persisted in config.toml. Codex does not run a custom status-line script.

claude.title: Claude Code command
claude.body: Reads statusLine and subagentStatusLine from settings files. Commands can reference local scripts and may be disabled by disableAllHooks.

codex.title: Codex footer items
codex.body: Reads [tui].status_line from config.toml. Items such as model, directory, branch, tokens, rate limits, and task progress are selected and ordered.

statusLine.hidden: status_line is explicitly empty, so the Codex status line is hidden instead of using defaults.
statusLine.unknownItems: {{count}} unknown item(s) will be ignored by current Codex builds.
statusLine.redactedCommand: Sensitive command fragments are hidden in this view. Use View Raw to inspect the source file.

diagnostics.overridden: A higher-priority {{scope}} scope setting wins for this status line kind.
diagnostics.disabled: disableAllHooks is enabled in this settings file.
diagnostics.missingCommand: Claude Code statusLine does not contain a command.
diagnostics.unresolvedEntry: The command looks like a script path, but Berth did not confirm a readable local script.

defaultCodex.title: Codex default footer
defaultCodex.body: No tui.status_line setting was found, so Codex falls back to its built-in default footer items.

empty.all: No status line config was found. Claude Code uses settings.json command config; Codex falls back to Model + reasoning and Current directory when tui.status_line is unset.
empty.claude: No Claude Code statusLine or subagentStatusLine setting was found in the scanned settings files.
empty.codex: No Codex tui.status_line setting was found. Codex will use its default footer items unless the field is explicitly set.

mcp.title: External tools and data sources
mcp.summary: MCP servers expose tools, resources, and prompts through a shared protocol. They let an agent reach systems such as databases, issue trackers, files, and internal APIs.

points.role: Use MCP when a capability needs a real external system instead of static instructions.
points.scope: Scope tells you whether the server is personal, shared with a repo, or managed by policy.
points.review: Review exposed tools and environment variables because MCP can let the agent take real actions.

providers.claude: Claude Code reads MCP server definitions from settings and project MCP files.
providers.codex: Codex reads MCP servers from config.toml.
providers.abstract: The shared asset is an external tool or resource exposed through MCP.

hooks.title: Lifecycle automation
hooks.summary: Hooks are commands or handlers that run when the agent reaches a lifecycle moment, such as before a tool call, after a result, before compaction, or before stop.

points.role: Use hooks for checks, logging, guardrails, and context updates that should happen around agent actions.
points.scope: Each provider exposes a different event set, so Berth maps them into a shared lifecycle view.
points.review: Hook commands can run local code. Check the trigger, matcher, and entry file before enabling them.

providers.claude: Claude Code hooks are settings-backed commands attached to lifecycle events.
providers.codex: Codex hooks are config.toml command handlers around supported session and tool events.

plugins.title: Packaged capability bundles
plugins.summary: Plugins package multiple assets together, such as skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and settings. They are useful when a capability should be installed, versioned, and shared as one unit.

points.role: Use plugins for reusable distributions rather than one-off project configuration.
points.scope: Installed plugins may be user-level, project-level, or policy-managed depending on the provider.
points.review: Inspect manifests and bundled components before enabling a plugin from outside your team.

providers.claude: Claude Code plugins bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and settings.
providers.abstract: Berth treats plugins as installable capability bundles.

statusLine.title: Runtime status surface
statusLine.summary: Status line assets render compact context about the running session, such as model, directory, branch, cost, or task state.

points.role: Use this for glanceable state, not for long instructions or hidden automation.
points.scope: Status line support varies by provider, but the abstract asset is a readout attached to the agent UI.
points.review: Keep scripts fast and safe because they can run repeatedly while the session updates.

providers.claude: Claude Code status lines run configured commands and render their output.
providers.codex: Codex status lines select ordered built-in footer items from config.toml.

permissions.title: Runtime safety policy
permissions.summary: Permissions define what the agent runtime may do without asking, what must be confirmed, and what is blocked. They enforce boundaries outside the model prompt.

points.role: Use permissions to control tool use, file access, command execution, network access, and delegated agents.
points.scope: Rules can merge across user, project, local, and managed layers; higher policy may be impossible to override.
points.review: Broad allow rules and bypass modes reduce prompts but increase risk. Prefer narrow rules for trusted workflows.

providers.claude: Claude Code permissions define allow, ask, deny, and bypass behavior around tools.
providers.codex: Codex combines approval policy, sandbox mode, and explicit permissions.

env.title: Session and subprocess environment
env.summary: Environment variables configure the agent process, hooks, MCP servers, telemetry, and provider integrations. They often carry feature flags or references to secrets.

points.role: Use env vars when runtime behavior depends on local machine, provider, or integration settings.
points.scope: Some variables apply to every session; others are forwarded only to an MCP server or subprocess.
points.review: Berth should show names and sources, not secret values. Treat variables containing keys or tokens as sensitive.

providers.claude: Claude Code can define session environment through settings and integration config.
providers.codex: Codex environment behavior is controlled by config and shell environment policy.
providers.abstract: The shared asset is process environment visible to the agent or its subprocesses.

hooks.filteredHint: Filters only change the hook rows. Lifecycle explanations stay visible so you can still understand where each stage sits.

comparison.title: Lifecycle comparison
comparison.body: Use this view to compare which native events each visible agent exposes under the same abstract stage.

intro.title: What are hooks?
intro.all: Hooks are local scripts or handlers that run when an agent reaches a specific moment, such as starting a session, receiving your prompt, using a tool, compacting context, or stopping. This view combines Claude Code and Codex into one lifecycle and calls out where their behavior differs.
intro.claude: Hooks are Claude Code handlers that run around session setup, user prompts, tool use, permissions, notifications, and shutdown. This view only shows Claude Code stages and scanned Claude Code hook files.
intro.codex: Hooks are Codex command handlers that run around sessions, user prompts, supported tool use, permission requests, compaction, subagents, and stop. This view only shows Codex stages and scanned Codex hook files.

trigger.title: Trigger point
trigger.body: A hook does not run all the time. It runs when the agent reaches its matching behavior.

handler.title: Handler
handler.body: Most hooks eventually execute a command or script from a config file.

body.all: The same event name can mean different coverage. Codex PreToolUse only covers Bash, apply_patch, and MCP tools.
body.claude: This view only describes Claude Code hooks, so cross-agent differences are hidden until you switch back to All.
body.codex: This view only describes Codex hooks, so cross-agent differences are hidden until you switch back to All.

health.title: Hook checks
health.detailsBody: These checks come from the same health scanner as Overview, filtered to hooks and the current Agent view.
health.loadingDetail: Berth is reading hook scanner results for the current Agent view.
health.staleDetail: Showing previous hook checks while Berth refreshes hook checks for this Agent view.
health.okDetail: No hook health checks need attention for this view.

severityDetail.error: These hook checks need a configuration fix before the hook can be trusted.
severityDetail.warning: These hook checks may still run, but Berth found a risk or a missing platform-specific setting.
severityDetail.info: These hook checks are informational and do not block hook usage.

recovery.title: Recovery center
recovery.emptyBody: Berth has no disabled Claude Code hook restore points to show.
recovery.confirmRestore: Restore this Claude Code hook? Berth will write it back to {{sourcePath}}. Event: {{event}}. Hook: {{summary}}
recovery.confirmClear: Clear this restore point? Berth will only remove the sidecar entry and will not edit {{sourcePath}}. Event: {{event}}. Hook: {{summary}}

statusDetail.recoverable: This restore point can be written back to the source file.
statusDetail.source-missing: The source file is missing. Restore is disabled until the file exists again.
statusDetail.already-restored: An equivalent hook already exists in the source file. You can clear the restore point.
statusDetail.invalid: Berth cannot inspect this restore point safely.

session-start.title: Session starts
session-start.behavior: The agent opens or resumes a conversation and prepares the first context it will use.
session-start.guide: Use this stage for setup work: inject context, check local state, or prepare rules before the agent starts acting.

user-input.title: User input arrives
user-input.behavior: Your prompt has been submitted, but the agent has not started reasoning over it yet.
user-input.guide: Use this stage to validate or enrich user input before it reaches the model.

tool-before.title: Before a tool runs
tool-before.behavior: The agent is about to run a shell command, edit files, or call a supported external tool.
tool-before.guide: Use this stage for guardrails, logging, or checks that need to happen before a tool can make changes.

permission.title: Permission is requested
permission.behavior: The agent needs approval or an explicit answer before it can continue.
permission.guide: Use this stage to inspect approval requests and keep sensitive actions visible.

tool-after.title: After a tool runs
tool-after.behavior: A tool has returned output, succeeded, failed, or finished as part of a batch.
tool-after.guide: Use this stage to review results, capture logs, or ask the agent to react to tool output.

subagent.title: Subagent work
subagent.behavior: The main agent starts, monitors, or stops delegated work.
subagent.guide: Use this stage to pass context to subagents, audit delegated work, or keep them running when more work is needed.

context-maintenance.title: Context maintenance
context-maintenance.behavior: The agent compacts conversation context or observes configuration, instruction, directory, or file changes.
context-maintenance.guide: Use this stage to preserve important context and respond when the working environment changes.

session-stop.title: Agent stops
session-stop.behavior: The agent is about to finish a turn, stop a run, fail to stop cleanly, or end the session.
session-stop.guide: Use this stage for final checks, summaries, or follow-up instructions before the agent becomes idle.

environment.title: Environment events
environment.behavior: The surrounding workspace changes, a worktree is created or removed, or the agent sends a notification.
environment.guide: Use this stage for workspace-level events that are outside the normal prompt and tool loop.

claude.summary: Claude Code can run setup and session-start hooks when it prepares a session.

codex.summary: Codex supports SessionStart when a session starts, resumes, clears, or continues after compaction.

claude.summary: Claude Code can run hooks before user input is submitted and when prompt expansion occurs.

codex.summary: Codex supports UserPromptSubmit before the prompt reaches the model.

claude.summary: Claude Code PreToolUse covers a broad tool surface, including file, shell, web, and MCP tools.

codex.summary: Codex PreToolUse is available for supported shell, patch, and MCP tool calls.

claude.summary: Claude Code exposes permission requests, denials, and elicitation events.

codex.summary: Codex exposes PermissionRequest when it is about to ask for approval.

claude.summary: Claude Code separates successful tool output, failed tool output, and tool batches.

codex.summary: Codex uses PostToolUse for supported tool output, including some failed command output.

claude.summary: Claude Code exposes subagents, tasks, and teammate idle events.

codex.summary: Codex exposes subagent start and stop events.

claude.summary: Claude Code exposes compaction plus instruction, config, cwd, and file change events.

codex.summary: Codex exposes hooks before and after context compaction.

claude.summary: Claude Code can react to stop, stop failure, and session end events.

codex.summary: Codex supports Stop before the main agent finishes a turn.

claude.summary: Claude Code supports notification and worktree events.

codex.summary: Codex does not expose a hook event for this stage.

unknown.description: Berth has not mapped this event yet.

Setup.description: Runs while Claude Code prepares session setup.

SessionStart.description: Runs when a session starts, resumes, or continues after context changes.

UserPromptSubmit.description: Runs after you submit a prompt and before the model receives it.

UserPromptExpansion.description: Runs when Claude Code expands prompt content.

PreToolUse.description: Runs before a supported tool call executes.

PermissionRequest.description: Runs when the agent is about to ask for approval.

PermissionDenied.description: Runs when a Claude Code permission request is denied.

Elicitation.description: Runs when Claude Code asks for structured user input.

ElicitationResult.description: Runs when Claude Code receives structured user input.

PostToolUse.description: Runs after supported tool output is available.

PostToolUseFailure.description: Runs after a Claude Code tool fails.

PostToolBatch.description: Runs after a Claude Code tool batch completes.

SubagentStart.description: Runs when delegated agent work starts.

SubagentStop.description: Runs when delegated agent work is about to stop.

TaskCreated.description: Runs when Claude Code creates a task.

TaskCompleted.description: Runs when Claude Code completes a task.

TeammateIdle.description: Runs when a Claude Code teammate becomes idle.

InstructionsLoaded.description: Runs when Claude Code loads instructions.

ConfigChange.description: Runs when Claude Code observes config changes.

CwdChanged.description: Runs when Claude Code changes working directory.

FileChanged.description: Runs when Claude Code observes file changes.

Stop.description: Runs before the main agent stops the current turn.

StopFailure.description: Runs when Claude Code fails to stop cleanly.

SessionEnd.description: Runs when a Claude Code session ends.

WorktreeCreate.description: Runs when Claude Code creates a worktree.

WorktreeRemove.description: Runs when Claude Code removes a worktree.

Notification.description: Runs when Claude Code sends a user notification.

limitations.codexToolCoverage: Codex only applies tool hooks to Bash, apply_patch, and MCP tools. It does not cover every tool-like action.
limitations.codexPostToolMerged: Codex does not split successful and failed tool output into separate hook events.

codex.unsupported: Codex has no hooks equivalent for Claude Code notification or worktree events.

emptyStage.title: No hook is configured for this stage.
emptyStage.body: The agent can still pass through this behavior. Berth keeps the stage visible so the lifecycle remains readable.

unknown.title: Unmapped events
unknown.body: These hooks use event names Berth does not know yet. They are shown here instead of being hidden.

actions.noOpenTargets: No openable file target was detected.

management.noTargetPath: No file path is available for this action.
management.noEntryFile: No local script entry was detected in this command.
management.managedHook: This hook is managed by policy or an external source, so Berth cannot disable it here.
management.claudeSingleHookUserOnly: Berth currently supports soft-disable only for user-level Claude Code hooks.
management.codexSingleHookNotConnected: Codex can disable non-managed hooks in its hook browser, but Berth has not wired that write path yet.
management.singleHookMissingKey: Berth could not compute a stable hook key for this row, so it cannot change this hook safely.
management.unknownAgent: Berth does not know how this agent stores hook state.
management.projectReadOnly: Project-level hook switches are shown for review only. Edit the source file directly.
management.codexUnsupportedHookType: Codex currently parses this hook type but does not run it as a command hook.
management.codexAsyncHookSkipped: Codex currently skips async hook handlers.
management.confirmEnableHook: Enable this Codex hook? Berth will update hooks.state in your user config. Source: {{path}}
management.confirmDisableHook: Disable this Codex hook? Berth will update hooks.state in your user config. Source: {{path}}
management.confirmRestoreClaudeHook: Restore this Claude Code hook? Berth will write it back from the restore point into user settings. Event: {{event}}. Command: {{command}}. Disabled at: {{disabledAt}}. Source: {{path}}
management.confirmSoftDisableClaudeHook: Disable this Claude Code hook? Berth will remove the hook from user settings, then keep a restore point and backup. Event: {{event}}. Command: {{command}}. Source: {{path}}
management.errorStaleTarget: This hook was changed or removed by another edit. Refresh before trying again.
management.errorTargetChanged: This hook changed while Berth was preparing the update. Refresh the Hooks view before trying again.
management.errorSourceChanged: This hook source kept changing during the update. Wait for the other write to finish, then refresh and try again.
management.errorRestorePointMissing: No restore point was found for this hook. It may already be restored or the restore record was removed.

agentPluginCapabilityDetails.claudeHookSchema: Claude Code exposes command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, and agent hook handlers; Berth still renders parts of the hook UI through existing code.

agentPluginCapabilityDetails.claudeHookActions: Claude Code user hook toggles use soft removal plus a Berth sidecar restore point. Project and managed hooks stay read-only.
agentPluginCapabilityDetails.codexHookActions: Codex user hook toggles update hooks.state in config.toml. Project and managed hooks stay read-only.
agentPluginCapabilityDetails.healthChecksNotPluginOwned: Health checks are available today, but their rules still live in the health engine instead of the plugin registry.
agentPluginCapabilityDetails.manifestAdapterMetadataOnly: The manifest declares asset descriptors. Runtime exposes metadata and source coverage without executing third-party code.
agentPluginCapabilityDetails.manifestMetadataOnly: The manifest is visible in the registry, but it has no executable adapter or concrete source descriptors.
agentPluginCapabilityDetails.thirdPartyCodeNotExecuted: The manifest declares an adapter entrypoint. Berth records it but does not import or execute third-party code.
agentPluginCapabilityDetails.uiGuidanceInProgress: Settings uses this plugin metadata now. Other pages still have Agent-specific presentation code.
